items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: And when I was playing with Paul Whiteman’s group I took stuff back to him.

ctx.x: Man. Let me return to your own career here for a minute. The sixties were quite an amazing era for you it seems. I don’t know if you can divide it into just the sixties, but you played with a long, long list. Does anybody stand out in your own mind, particular tours or recordings that you’d just like to mention?

All of it really. I mean it all is — each entity is one component or one part — when I say sum of the parts that’s the reason why like my first album that I produced is called “Sum” S-U-M “of the Parts.” Because I recognized that I’m the sum total of all these influences, all these people, everything that I’ve studied, everything that I’ve dedicated myself to in terms of my spirituality, my learning, my friendships with people and just trying to understand what the totality of life is all about.
